lines.text: By one hundred thousand years ago, people kept their knowledge in stories.
A hunter tells of the river that runs when the others dry where the water hides.
That night, the story is copied into every memory.
A story is information that copies itself by being heard.
Children retell it, and theirs. The hunter dies; his knowledge lives.
A body passed knowledge to a few. A story passes it to everyone.
But the story has an enemy: forgetting.
Tell it once, and it fades in every head at once no original to check.
So say it plainly: the story was the first backup. One memory became many, hard to kill.
The first archive was a body. The second, a story everyone heard.
Chapter two of how information evolved on Earth. Subscribe, like, follow Earth One.
